work.abstract_text: Using Munagi's residue-class criterion (2008, Theorem 3.1) and extending Flowers and Lockard's construction (2021, Lemma 4.2, p. 467), we answer Questions 5.12–5.14 of Dietz, Flowers and Lockard's A study of m-ary partitions whose conjugates are q-ary (2026, §5, p. 404) in their self-conjugate setting: among conjugate m-ary partitions, the first odd exponent admitting a self-conjugate partition for even m is m+1, the first exponent admitting a non-square self-conjugate partition for any m is m+1, and odd exponents are impossible for odd m. A row-multiplicity identity gives N ≡ H+W−1 modulo (m−1)(q−1) for conjugate (m,q)-ary partitions. For partitions of m^r it yields a positive exponent defect divisible by m−1 whenever the diagram is not rectangular. This proves the exact nonrectangular threshold and, with the credited constructions, classifies all exponents admitting a non-square self-conjugate partition.

work.title: Sharp thresholds for Dietz, Flowers and Lockard's self-conjugate partition questions: extending Flowers and Lockard's construction
